messages:
Aisha: Heads-up — I'm going to run an experiment tomorrow: "graceful-deny + probe-token lane" for overloaded queues. Idea: instead of wholesale soft-429s we keep a tiny probe stream so kernels stay warm and KV locality doesn't collapse. Plan is to: 1) limit admitted tokens by normal token_budget, 2) allow a small fraction of probe tokens that bypass immediate shed but are sampled, 3) route probes to a diversity set of prefixes. Objections? :eyes:
Tom: Sounds interesting. Quick Q: how do you pick the probe budget? last time a fixed token budget caused tail spikes when probes lined up with big batches. :thinking:
Aisha: Good point. We'll use a percentile-driven target + an absolute cap. Start conservative: probe_fraction = 0.02 (2% of admitted tokens) and probe_max_tokens_per_sec = 10. If p99 latency stays below target we nudge to 4%.
Ravi: KV cache note: probes that hit the same hot prefixes will pollute the cache and evict useful entries. Probes need to be prefix-diverse and maybe avoid top-N hottest keys.
Aisha: Agreed — will stratify sampling by prefix hash bucket and exclude keys in the hot-key blacklist. Also probes will carry a hint so the runtime can prefer kernel paths that are safe to prefetch.
Marta: Rollout suggestion: canary 5% on staging-dedicated / 1 replica of dedicated hardware. Dashboards to watch: p95/p99 latency, kv_hit_rate, average batch_size, kernel_mismatch_rate, 429_rate, and probe_success_rate. Alert if kernel_mismatch_rate > 5% or p99 regresses > 10%. :thumbsup:
Tom: Do you have local perf numbers from the synthetic replay? curious about kernel warmup cost vs benefit.
Tom: ```
# local replay summary
baseline: p95=120ms p99=320ms avg_batch=8 kv_hit=0.42 kernel_switches=18/h
with-probe(2%): p95=118ms p99=305ms avg_batch=7.9 kv_hit=0.43 kernel_switches=6/h
notes: probe reduced kernel switches and improved p99 slightly, no obvious batch bloat
```
admit-bot: preflight-check: canary quota=OK, probe-config-valid=OK, smoke-tests=PASS. Metrics hook created at /dashboards/probe-experiment.
Aisha: Updated admission config draft (will open PR):
```json
{
  "admission_mode": "graceful_deny",
  "probe_fraction": "0.02",
  "probe_max_tokens_per_sec": "10",
  "token_budget_window_ms": "1000",
  "soft_reject_threshold": "0.85",
  "prefix_sampling_buckets": "32",
  "exclude_hot_key_top_n": "10"
}
```
Ravi: Also: when soft_reject triggers, prefer degrading to quantized/int8 kernel or narrower beam instead of full deny. That preserves some correctness while reducing cost. We should add a kernel-fallback-policy mapping to the admission rule.
Marta: I'll draft the rollout doc + the playbook for rollback + add the dashboard panels. @Aisha can you add the failure cases and prometheus alerts to the PR?
Aisha: Will do. I'll push the PR tonight and schedule the 5% canary for 09:00 PT tomorrow. If anyone wants to join the canary watch ping me. Thanks for the quick feedback! :pray:
Tom: Nice — will be on watch. If we see sudden kv_hit drop we should be able to flip probe_fraction -> 0 quickly.
Ravi: Also instrument per-prefix eviction churn metric — that'll tell us whether probes are causing cache thrash.
Aisha: Good call. Adding eviction_churn and probe_key_entropy to the telemetry list. Closing loop tomorrow post-canary with perf logs and kernel-selection traces.
